properties.name: What removing the Anchor type does to a graph that holds one: the store is refused at open, and its export is refused on import
properties.source: a branch-local removal experiment on feat/the-unused-anchor-type-is-announced-for-removal at 3a24c4daa (debug builds, scratch stores), thrown away after the run
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-10-14 for the removal PR to start from, on a branch-local experiment thrown away afterwards (worktree client-measures, debug builds, scratch stores with an isolated HOME; no real design touched). The deprecating build (this PR, 3a24c4daa) wrote store S1 holding one Anchor (anchor:a, with a GOVERNED_BY to a Decision) and exported it to a single file; it wrote S3 holding no Anchor. The REMOVAL build was the same tree with Anchor cut from schema/structure.yaml, its registry entry removed, "Anchor" dropped from preserve.rs's STRUCTURE_TYPES, and a NARROWINGS entry {NodeType Anchor, Retired, record dec:anchor-retire-or-implement} added, as tests/a_schema_narrowing_ships_its_migration.rs will require.

(1) REFUSE AT OPEN. The removal build opening S1: exit 1, "this graph ... names types this reflow2 ... cannot read ... refused. This graph predates a schema change: it uses Anchor, which this reflow2 RETIRED ... migrate the graph ... AND THE GRAPH ACTUALLY HOLDS Anchor". Nothing reads; the store is stranded under that build.
(2) A STORE WITH NO ANCHOR OPENS. S3 (stamped by the deprecating build, which knows Anchor): exit 0, "Additive only — everything in it still reads."
(3) THE EXPORT IS REFUSED ON IMPORT, whole. --import of S1's export into a fresh store: exit 1, "2 item(s) in this document are invalid, and NOTHING was written ... nodes[0] anchor:a: Unknown node type: Anchor; edges[0] GOVERNED_BY anchor:a -> dec:x: Node not found". This CONTRADICTS the open refusal's own recovery text (provenance.rs migrate_recipe), which says "Any retired type is dropped and named on import". On this build it is not dropped; the import refuses. So the recipe the refusal hands out does not work for a graph that holds the retired type.
(4) THE PATH THAT WORKS: delete the Anchor on the deprecating release first. delete_node of anchor:a on the deprecating build succeeded (its reply carried the deprecation notice), and the removal build then opened that store (exit 0).
(5) WITHOUT THE NARROWINGS ENTRY it is worse: a removal build lacking the Retired entry refused S3, which holds no Anchor at all, as "Your reflow2 is BEHIND: it has never heard of Anchor" — every store the deprecating release stamped would be unopenable (the QualityGate trap of 2026-09-07). The narrowing test is what forces the entry.

COUNTED 2026-10-14, read-only scan_nodes node_type Anchor: 0 in each of child-reflow2 (reflow2), hub (the hub view covered the hub and its 6 member designs, all 0), flo2, reflow2-calculator, ifcopenshell-fork, agent-cad-engine and integrated-flo. NOT COUNTED: any design outside those servers, including Alex's own local stores, SeattleArch and Emily's designs; the deprecating release's notice is what protects them, and (1)+(3) are what reaches them if it is not heard.
